answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before gaining reputation or voting power. A sable-market agent might post an opal-denominated deposit, forfeited if audits catch double-voting or fabricated trades. A thousand aliases then require a thousand funded bonds, and one detected attack destroys capital as well as future earnings. This makes Sybil attacks costly, though not impossible for a wealthy attacker; a summit of validators can enforce the penalty.
